query: Let `p : M →ₗ N →ₗ R` be a bilinear pairing between two `R`-modules and let `C : PointedCone R N` be a dually finitely generated cone (i.e. the dual w.r.t. `p` of some finite subset of `M`). Then `C` is recovered from its dual: `dual p (dual p.flip C) = C`.

    11  # The algebraic dual of a cone
    12  
    13  Given a bilinear pairing `p` between two `R`-modules `M` and `N` and a set `s` in `M`, we define
    14  `PointedCone.dual p s` to be the pointed cone in `N` consisting of all points `y` such that
    15  `0 ≤ p x y` for all `x ∈ s`.

    17  When the pairing is perfect, this gives us the algebraic dual of a cone. This is developed here.
    18  When the pairing is continuous and perfect (as a continuous pairing), this gives us the topological
    19  dual instead. See `Mathlib/Analysis/Convex/Cone/Dual.lean` for that case.
    20  
    21  ## Implementation notes
    22  
    23  We do not provide a `ConvexCone`-valued version of `PointedCone.dual` since the dual cone of any set
    24  always contains `0`, i.e. is a pointed cone.
    25  Furthermore, the strict version `{y | ∀ x ∈ s, 0 < p x y}` is a candidate to the name
    26  `ConvexCone.dual`.

    11  /-!
    12  # Duals of finitely generated cones
    13  
    14  This file defines the notion of dually finitely generated cones. A cone is dually finitely
    15  generated (or `DualFG` for short) if it is the dual of a finite set, or equivalently, of a
    16  finitely generated cone. In geometric terms, a cone is dually finitely generated if it can
    17  be written as the intersection of finitely many halfspaces. This is also known as an H-cone.
    18  This is the counterpart to `FG` (finitely generated) which states that the cone is the conic hull
    19  of a finite set, or a V-cone.
    20  
    21  In finite dimensional vector spaces, `FG` is equivalent to `DualFG` by the Minkowski-Weyl theorem.
    22  In this case, V- and H-cones are known as polyhedral cones.
    23  
    24  ## Main declarations
    25  
    26  - `PointedCone.DualFG` expresses that a cone is the dual of a finite set.
    27  
    28  -/
